annotations.title: Commercial property and land sale prices actually paid

description: Use this when a user asks what shops, offices, workshops, warehouses or other commercial premises actually sold for, or what a plot of non-farm land (a building plot) sold for, per square metre, in a town or postcode, in France (country FR), Hong Kong (country HK), Sweden (country SE), Singapore (country SG), Taiwan (country TW) or New York City (country US). Returns the median price per square metre, a typical range (10th–90th percentile), the number of sales, the period covered, a confidence label, and the official source and licence, from government sale records (prices paid, not asking prices). How fresh: France: twice a year, with a delay of several months; Hong Kong: yearly, published about 5 months after the year ends (2025 figures published June 2026); Sweden: yearly; sales during 2025, published 5 June 2026; Singapore: a historic file: awards from 1992 to mid-2016 only, last updated by the publisher on 6 June 2024. Every answer states its period; Taiwan: every 10 days. A sale appears one to two months after the deal; answers cover whole calendar months ending at least 30 days before the newest deal; New York City: monthly, around the 15th, with sales recorded through the end of the prior month. Do not use for homes, farmland, rents, asking prices or listings, the value of one particular building, or other countries.

basis.description: HK only: price (default, average sale price per m²) or rent (average monthly rent per m²).

country.description: FR = France (DVF); HK = Hong Kong (Rating and Valuation Department, yearly average price per m² of private offices, retail premises and flatted factories, official statistic); SE = Sweden (official yearly average price of sold industrial property by county, per property); SG = Singapore (state-land tender awards 1992 to mid-2016, SGD per m² of gross floor area); TW = Taiwan; US = United States, New York City only

grade.description: HK offices only: A (default), B or C, the RVD office grade.

months.description: How many recent months to include. Default 24. HK: ignored; the figures are yearly (newest year with a usable figure). SE: ignored; the figures are yearly (latest year with at least 5 sales). SG: look-back in months from the newest award in the file (July 2016), e.g. 120. Leave out for the whole file (1993 to 2016). TW: 12 or 24 whole calendar months; up to 18 gives 12 (24 if a place has too few sales in 12), more gives 24. US: up to 12 months (the city's file holds the last 12).

postcode.description: Postcode, for a precise area. FR: 5-digit postcode, e.g. '33000'; use instead of town for a precise area. HK: not used (Hong Kong has no postcodes). SE: not supported; give the county as town. SG: not supported; give the planning area as town. TW: not supported (the register has no postcodes); give the city, county or district as town. US: 5-digit New York City ZIP code, e.g. '10017'.

premises.description: HK only: office (default when town is an office district), retail (default for a region) or factory (flatted factories).

property_type.description: commercial = shops, offices, workshops and other commercial or industrial premises (default); land = building plots and other non-farm land sold without a building. FR: commercial (default) or land. Alsace-Moselle and Mayotte are not covered. HK: commercial (default) = private offices, retail premises and flatted factories; land is not available. Use premises to choose which. SE: commercial (default) = sold industrial real estate (factories, petrol stations and workshops, warehouses). land is not available for Sweden. SG: land only (state-owned development sites sold by tender; price per m² of gross floor area). Leave out or use land. TW: commercial (default; shops, offices, factories, per m² of building) or land (building plots without a building, per m² of land). US: commercial (default; offices, stores, lofts, factories, garages, warehouses) or land (commercial vacant land).

town.description: Town or city. FR: town, e.g. 'Bordeaux', or use postcode. HK: required. Offices: a district (Central, Sheung Wan, Wan Chai, Causeway Bay, North Point, Quarry Bay, Tsim Sha Tsui, Mong Kok, Kwun Tong). Retail or factories: a region ('Hong Kong' for Hong Kong Island, 'Kowloon', 'New Territories'). SE: a county ('Skåne', 'Stockholm', 'Västra Götaland', 'Östergötland'); leave out for the whole of Sweden. Counties, not towns. SG: a URA planning area, e.g. Bedok, Downtown Core, Geylang, Woodlands, Queenstown, River Valley. Leave out for all of Singapore. At least 5 sites must match. TW: a city or county in English or Chinese ('Taipei', 'New Taipei', 'Taichung', 'Kaohsiung', '臺北市'), or a district with its city ("Zhongshan, Taipei", '臺北市中山區'). Omit for all of Taiwan. US: a New York City borough ('Manhattan', 'Brooklyn') or neighborhood ('Midtown East', 'SoHo'); omit for the whole city, or use postcode.

name: pricepaid_commercial_property

outputSchema.description: A price answer: a range or an official statistic with sample size, period, confidence, source and licence.

answer_id.description: Audit trail: a stable id (hash of source id, normalised query, data period and method_version). The same question on the same data gives the same id; keep it with the reasoning that used the figure.

as_of.description: When the answer was produced (ISO 8601); the snapshot date when the official source was down and the answer comes from our copy.

data_age_days.description: Whole days between data_as_of and retrieved_at; null when data_as_of is null.

data_as_of.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) of the newest data point behind the figure; null when unknown.

evidence.description: Audit trail: what kind of evidence the figure is.

label.description: Short name of the kind of evidence, e.g. 'Recorded sale prices', 'Official published average', 'Official published index', 'Posted shelf or pump price', 'Posted or listed price', 'Contract award value', 'Regulated reimbursement price'.

meaning.description: One sentence on what this kind of evidence does and does not establish.

extra.description: Source-specific details (for example cheapest stations). extra.stale is true when the answer comes from our copy of the source.

method_version.description: Audit trail: version of the way this source turns raw data into an answer (per source, default '1').

notice.description: Information, not a valuation or offer. Also says when the answer is our copy because the official source did not respond.

period.description: The period the records cover (ISO dates), or the date of the snapshot when the answer comes from our copy.

anyOf.description: The price. Null when there is not enough data to publish a figure (fewer than 5 records) or nothing matched.

measure.description: What value is: median for ranges built from records; average or median for official statistics.

typical_high.description: 90th percentile; null for official statistics that give no range.

typical_low.description: 10th percentile; null for official statistics that give no range.

unit.description: What the price is per, e.g. 'per litre', 'per home', 'per kWh'.

value.description: The headline figure. For ranges built from records it equals median.

price_type.description: transaction, posted_pump_price, posted_price, contract_price, reimbursement_price or official_statistic.

query.description: The request as understood, echoed back.

reliability.description: How far to trust the figure as a distribution of real prices. official_with_count = a published official figure with a record count; official_median_no_count = a published average or median with no record count (confidence 'high' there means the publisher is official, not that a count was checked); record_level = 15+ records we hold; thin = 5–14 records; stale = our copy because the official source did not respond; insufficient_data = no figure published.

retrieved_at.description: Audit trail: when ProofPrice produced this answer (ISO 8601). For an answer from our own copy this is now, while as_of is the snapshot date.

sample_size.description: Number of records behind the figure; null when the publisher does not say.

source.description: Where the figure comes from, under which licence, and the attribution line to show.

attribution.description: The attribution line to show with the figure.

url.description: The publisher's page for this data.

statistic.description: Official statistics only: what kind of figure it is and the period the publisher states it for.

status.description: ok = a figure is returned; insufficient_data = fewer than 5 matching records; no_matches = nothing matched.

suggestions.description: Short plain things to try next: widen the period or area, ask for an itemised quote. May be empty.

summary.description: One plain sentence an AI can quote.
